Interior plan · 2026

Our Japandi apartment plan

How we want to set up the apartment: light oak, linen and paper lanterns, low seating, a projector instead of a TV, and a lot of built-in storage so the rooms stay calm. These are simple 3D sketches of the layout and furniture, not photo renders.

  • ≈ 85 m²
  • ceiling 2.63 m
  • full-height windows
  • 2 bedrooms → bedroom + tinker room
OverviewFloor planLivingKitchen & diningBedroomBathroomTinker roomBalcony
全体

The whole apartment

Kitchen, dining nook and living room share the balcony end. The bedroom and tinker room sit along the window wall, with the genkan, pantry, WC, laundry and bathroom along the hall.

居間

Living room and home cinema

A low L-sofa with a chaise to lie on, and a kotatsu in front, so the sofa doubles as a backrest when you sit on the floor. Oak acoustic slats run behind the sofa. The XGIMI projector sits on a turntable in a slatted oak niche, so it can throw onto the bedroom wall or swing round to the dining nook wall. Three paper lanterns hang over the kotatsu, outside the beam.

  • ≈ 17.5 m²
  • 113″ on the living wall
  • 91″ on the nook wall
  • sofa seat h 38 cm
台所

Kitchen and dining nook

A compact kitchen with a 2 m counter-height peninsula that works as extra worktop and storage. On the other side is a built-in booth with benches on all four sides of a square table, like a raised tatami corner. It seats six, and the living-side bench slides out to get in.

  • kitchen ≈ 6 m²
  • nook ≈ 7 m²
  • peninsula 60 × 200
  • booth 175 × 175
  • table 90 × 90
寝室

Bedroom with a hidden walk-in

The bed is centred with the door swing kept clear. The walk-in closet is built from furniture, not walls: two cabinets with slatted oak backs face the bed, so from the bed it reads as furniture. The entrance is a noren at the window end, out of sight from the door. The cabinet facing the bed is a shallow 22 cm closet for small things.

  • bedroom ≈ 11 m²
  • walk-in ≈ 3.4 m²
  • bed 160 × 200
風呂

Japanese-style bathroom

Split into a dry room and a wet room. The dry room has a double vanity with two basins, a mirror cabinet and a tall cabinet for toiletries. A thin new wall with a glass slider leads to the wet room, where the whole floor can get wet: shower and hinoki stool first, then a soak in the tub.

  • dry room 2.6 m²
  • wet room 4.2 m²
  • vanity 140 cm, 2 basins
工房

Tinker, work-from-home and woodworking room

A 2 m desk for two along the bedroom wall, with the window kept clear. A three-panel shoji slides across the full depth of the room to close off the workshop half, sealed so soldering fumes stay on that side. The workshop has an L-shaped bench with pegboard on both walls, and the 3D printer on a pull-out shelf under the bench. A closet by the door holds the 10″ network rack, and there is a floor cushion by the window for crocheting.

  • ≈ 10.2 m²
  • desk 200 × 72
  • bench 192 + 60 cm
  • shoji 3 × ≈ 68 cm
縁側

Balcony

An enclosed balcony with clad side walls and a glass railing. Two low teak lounge chairs with cord seats and linen cushions face the view across a low teak table. A charred cedar (yakisugi) planter runs the full width along the railing, with grasses and a small Japanese maple.

  • ≈ 6.1 m²
  • planter 307 × 34, h 45
  • chairs seat h 32

The renders are simplified block models to show layout, proportions and materials. Exact finishes, fabrics and light will look softer in real life.
